title: Critters 2: The Main Course
review: Starting off with a decent rationalisation of the total chaos at the end of {Critters}, and how the townsfolk have dealt with it in the long run. This is the real {Stranger Things}; a contemporary portrait of small town America in the 80s, and not just a parade of all the pop media that's still marketable, drenched in modern superhero quips. As the titular critters get loose it descends into exactly more of the silly chaos I hoped for. It goes full {Red Dwarf}, verging on being a {Wet Hot American Summer} style parody of its own subgenre. It's a bit of a shame the bounty hunters no longer have a comical misunderstanding of human culture, but at least they get their own storyline and character development again. This film taught me of the existence of carob.
spoilers: It's a shame they weren't brave enough to kill off Charlie. He sacrificed himself to save so many people. From the town clown to the hero they needed, it should have ended with the unveiling of a Charlie memorial statue outside the church.
